summary.text: A 67-year-old Hispanic woman with hypertension and chronic hyperlipidemia presented in June 2016 with a band-like bilateral headache, blurred vision, dizziness, light-headedness and nausea, without fever, vomiting or diarrhea.

Workup showed elevated serum protein, an M spike with IgM kappa, a lymphoplasmacytic bone marrow infiltrate, deletion 1p on FISH and splenomegaly; no other lytic lesions, organomegaly or lymphadenopathy, and a negative PET-CT. Findings were consistent with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and she was treated for clinical hyperviscosity syndrome.

She received plasmapheresis twice and then multiple cycles of bortezomib, dexamethasone and rituximab over seven months; the M-spike became undetectable, IgM fell to 76 mg/dL, splenomegaly resolved and headaches and visual disturbances stopped.
Treatment was taxing on her emotional well-being, resulting in depression, anxiety and hopelessness, and she was started on psychotherapy.
